```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "The 90-day goal only needs one paying customer. A consumer subscription at $8–20/month can be sold self-serve through an app store with no per-customer contract. B needs a HIPAA BAA executed with every customer and must win physician trust in AI-drafted notes that carry liability.",
    "B's brief documents a near-identical precedent, Cydoc, run by a clinically credentialed founder. It reached only four paying customers, $27,900 in 2024 revenue (mostly non-subscription), and $4,000–$6,000 integration cost per practice before shutting down. Its first sales call showed customers renegotiating scope per practice, which points to a slow, custom sales cycle that is hostile to a 90-day timeline.",
    "B's documented acquisition channel, conference exhibiting, costs $1,850–$10,000 per show and is event-gated. A's sourced channels include Apple Search Ads at about $3.76 CPA, which lets a solo operator test cheaply and quickly. A's figures are sufficient for a first paying customer even though the brief questions their long-term payback at $8/month.",
    "A's regulatory overhead is mostly one-time: a review of claims copy, a privacy policy, and age-gating. B's includes ongoing per-customer BAAs and safeguards plus FDA non-device scoping.",
    "A's competitors are largely free or freemium. Even so, Yoodli's published $8/$20 tiers and multiple live apps sourced in the brief show that consumers download and some pay in this category. A's demand quote from r/socialanxiety also names a specific gap that a narrow niche product could fill: chatbots don't give honest negative feedback."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's first demand quote is the weakest evidence in its brief. The PMHNP Reddit post complains that an employer never followed up on adding intake paperwork. It shows no willingness to pay for an AI intake or note tool, and the speaker is an employee, not the practice-owner payer. B's other demand point, the AMA after-hours EHR statistic, reaches the brief only secondhand through a competitor's marketing page. The claim that competitors have 'apparent traction' cites no source at all.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. A has serious gaps of its own. The brief admits the payer is undefined, pricing is not found for most competitors, Convo's ~$8 price rests on a single user review, and the category is crowded with free incumbents including a Stanford-backed one. B has a clearer payer and higher price point. A wins mainly because B's own brief contains strong, sourced evidence that this exact model sells slowly, and the question rewards speed to a first paying customer rather than long-term market size."
}
```
